q-35261.name: Question 1
q-35261.problem: Let $B=\{{b}_{1},{b}_{2}\}$ be a basis of ${R}^{2}$ and $[x]_{B}=[\begin{aligned}6 \\ 4\end{aligned}].$ What are the coordinates of $x$ relative to the basis $C=\{{c}_{1},{c}_{2}\},$ where ${c}_{1}=-8{b}_{2}$ and ${c}_{2}=3{b}_{1}?$
q-35261.worked_solution:
Since $[x]_{B}=[\begin{aligned}6 \\ 4\end{aligned}]$, we can write $x$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}x & =6{b}_{1}+4{b}_{2} \\  & =4{b}_{2}+6{b}_{1} \\  & =-(-4{b}_{2})+2(3{b}_{1}) \\  & =-\frac{1}{2}(-8{b}_{2})+2(3{b}_{1}) \\  & =-\frac{1}{2}{c}_{1}+2{c}_{2}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, $[x]_{C}=[\begin{aligned}-\frac{1}{2} \\ 2\end{aligned}].$

Let B={b1,b2} be a basis of R2 and [x]B=[64]. What are the coordinates of x relative to the basis C={c1,c2}, where c1=−8b2 and c2=3b1?

a
[x]C=[−2−4]
b
[x]C=[12−4]
c
[x]C=[−42]
d
[x]C=[−122]
e
[x]C=[4−12]
Submit
Incorrect
EXPLANATION

Since [x]B=[64], we can write x as follows:

x=6b1+4b2=4b2+6b1=−(−4b2)+2(3b1)=−12(−8b2)+2(3b1)=−12c1+2c2

Therefore, [x]C=[−122].

q-112632.name: Question 2
q-112632.problem: Let $C=\{{c}_{1},{c}_{2}\}$ be a basis of ${R}^{2}$ and $[x]_{C}=[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 1\end{aligned}].$ What are the coordinates of $x$ relative to the basis $B=\{{b}_{1},{b}_{2}\},$ where ${b}_{1}=\frac{1}{2}{c}_{2}$ and ${b}_{2}=-{c}_{1}?$
q-112632.worked_solution:
Since $[x]_{C}=[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 1\end{aligned}]$, we can write $x$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}x & =2{c}_{1}+{c}_{2} \\  & ={c}_{2}+2{c}_{1} \\  & =2(\frac{1}{2}{c}_{2})-2(-{c}_{1}) \\  & =2{b}_{1}-2{b}_{2}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, $[x]_{B}=[\begin{aligned}2 \\ -2\end{aligned}].$

Question 2
?

Let C={c1,c2} be a basis of R2 and [x]C=[21]. What are the coordinates of x relative to the basis B={b1,b2}, where b1=12c2 and b2=−c1?

a
[x]B=[−1−2].
b
[x]B=[−11].
c
[x]B=[2−1].
d
[x]B=[2−2]
e
[x]B=[−22].
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

Since [x]C=[21], we can write x as follows:

x=2c1+c2=c2+2c1=2(12c2)−2(−c1)=2b1−2b2

Therefore, [x]B=[2−2].

q-34773.name: Question 3
q-34773.problem: Let $C=\{{c}_{1},{c}_{2}\}$ be a basis of ${R}^{2}$ and $[x]_{C}=[\begin{aligned}-3 \\ -5\end{aligned}].$ What are the coordinates of $x$ relative to the basis $B=\{{b}_{1},{b}_{2}\},$ where ${b}_{1}=4{c}_{2}$ and ${b}_{2}=-2{c}_{1}?$
q-34773.worked_solution:
Since $[x]_{C}=[\begin{aligned}-3 \\ -5\end{aligned}]$, we can write $x$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}x & =-3{c}_{1}-5{c}_{2} \\  & =-5{c}_{2}-3{c}_{1} \\  & =-5({c}_{2})+3(-{c}_{1}) \\  & =-\frac{5}{4}(4{c}_{2})+\frac{3}{2}(-2{c}_{1}) \\  & =-\frac{5}{4}{b}_{1}+\frac{3}{2}{b}_{2}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, $[x]_{B}=[\begin{aligned}-\frac{5}{4} \\ \frac{3}{2}\end{aligned}].$

EXPLANATION

Since [x]C=[−3−5], we can write x as follows:

x=−3c1−5c2=−5c2−3c1=−5(c2)+3(−c1)=−54(4c2)+32(−2c1)=−54b1+32b2

q-35258.name: Question 4
q-35258.problem: Let $B=\{{b}_{1},{b}_{2}\}$ be a basis of ${R}^{2}$ and $[x]_{B}=[\begin{aligned}3 \\ -7\end{aligned}].$ What are the coordinates of $x$ relative to the basis $C=\{{c}_{1},{c}_{2}\},$ where ${c}_{1}=5{b}_{2}$ and ${c}_{2}=4{b}_{1}?$
q-35258.worked_solution:
Since $[x]_{B}=[\begin{aligned}3 \\ -7\end{aligned}]$, we can write $x$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}x & =3{b}_{1}-7{b}_{2} \\  & =-7{b}_{2}+3{b}_{1} \\  & =-\frac{7}{5}(5{b}_{2})+\frac{3}{4}(4{b}_{1}) \\  & =-\frac{7}{5}{c}_{1}+\frac{3}{4}{c}_{2}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, $[x]_{C}=[\begin{aligned}-\frac{7}{5} \\ \frac{3}{4}\end{aligned}].$

Question 4
?

Let B={b1,b2} be a basis of R2 and [x]B=[3−7]. What are the coordinates of x relative to the basis C={c1,c2}, where c1=5b2 and c2=4b1?

a
[x]C=[3475]
b
[x]C=[4534]
c
[x]C=[−45−54]
d
[x]C=[−7534]
e
[x]C=[75−34]
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

Since [x]B=[3−7], we can write x as follows:

x=3b1−7b2=−7b2+3b1=−75(5b2)+34(4b1)=−75c1+34c2

Therefore, [x]C=[−7534].

q-81219.name: Question 5
q-81219.problem: Let $C=\{{c}_{1},{c}_{2}\}$ be a basis of ${R}^{2}$ and $[x]_{C}=[\begin{aligned}-3 \\ 5\end{aligned}].$ What are the coordinates of $x$ relative to the basis $B=\{{b}_{1},{b}_{2}\},$ where ${b}_{1}=2{c}_{2}$ and ${b}_{2}=-5{c}_{1}?$
q-81219.worked_solution:
Since $[x]_{C}=[\begin{aligned}-3 \\ 5\end{aligned}]$, we can write $x$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}x & =-3{c}_{1}+5{c}_{2} \\  & =5{c}_{2}-3{c}_{1} \\  & =\frac{5}{2}(2{c}_{2})-\frac{3}{5}(5{c}_{1}) \\  & =\frac{5}{2}{b}_{1}+\frac{3}{5}{b}_{2}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, $[x]_{B}=[\begin{aligned}\frac{5}{2} \\ \frac{3}{5}\end{aligned}].$

Question 5
?

Let C={c1,c2} be a basis of R2 and [x]C=[−35]. What are the coordinates of x relative to the basis B={b1,b2}, where b1=2c2 and b2=−5c1?

a
[x]B=[−32−1]
b
[x]B=[3552]
c
[x]B=[52−35]
d
[x]B=[−52]
e
[x]B=[5235]
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

Since [x]C=[−35], we can write x as follows:

x=−3c1+5c2=5c2−3c1=52(2c2)−35(5c1)=52b1+35b2

Therefore, [x]B=[5235].

Let B={b1,b2,b3} be a basis of R3 and [x]B=[4−27]. What are the coordinates of x relative to the basis C={c1,c2,c3}, where c1=−b3, c2=12b1 and c3=2b2?

a
[x]C=[−78−1]
b
[x]C=[−4−472]
c
[x]C=[−1122]
d
[x]C=[72−4]
e
[x]C=[1−87]
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

Since [x]B=[4−27], we can write x as follows:

x=4b1−2b2+7b3=7b3+4b1−2b2=−7(−b3)+8(12b1)−(2b2)=−7c1+8c2−c3

Therefore, [x]C=[−78−1].

q-80814.name: Question 7
q-80814.problem: Let $B=\{{b}_{1},{b}_{2},{b}_{3}\}$ be a basis of ${R}^{3}$ and $[x]_{B}=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -3 \\ 6\end{aligned}].$ What are the coordinates of $x$ relative to the basis $C=\{{c}_{1},{c}_{2},{c}_{3}\},$ where ${c}_{1}=-{b}_{2}$, ${c}_{2}=2{b}_{3}$ and ${c}_{3}={b}_{1}?$
q-80814.worked_solution:
Since $[x]_{B}=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -3 \\ 6\end{aligned}]$, we can write $x$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}x & ={b}_{1}-3{b}_{2}+6{b}_{3} \\  & =-3{b}_{2}+6{b}_{3}+{b}_{1} \\  & =3(-{b}_{2})+3(2{b}_{3})+{b}_{1} \\  & =3{c}_{1}+3{c}_{2}+{c}_{3}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, $[x]_{C}=[\begin{aligned}3 \\ 3 \\ 1\end{aligned}].$

Question 7
?

Let B={b1,b2,b3} be a basis of R3 and [x]B=[1−36]. What are the coordinates of x relative to the basis C={c1,c2,c3}, where c1=−b2, c2=2b3 and c3=b1?

a
[x]C=[−321]
b
[x]C=[321]
c
[x]C=[331]
d
[x]C=[−331]
e
[x]C=[133]
Submit
Incorrect
EXPLANATION

Since [x]B=[1−36], we can write x as follows:

x=b1−3b2+6b3=−3b2+6b3+b1=3(−b2)+3(2b3)+b1=3c1+3c2+c3

Therefore, [x]C=[331].

Question 8

Let B={b1,b2,b3} be a basis of R3 and [x]B=[15−2418]. What are the coordinates of x relative to the basis C={c1,c2,c3}, where c1=3b2, c2=−6b3 and c3=3b1?

a
[x]C=[3−63]
b
[x]C=[546]
c
[x]C=[−35−8]
d
[x]C=[−583]
e
[x]C=[−8−35]
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

Since [x]B=[15−2418], we can write x as follows:

x=15b1−24b2+18b3=−24b2+18b3+15b1=−8(3b2)−3(−6b3)+5(3b1)=−8c1−3c2+5c3

Therefore, [x]C=[−8−35].

Question 9
?

Let B={b1,b2,b3} be a basis of R3 and [x]B=[110−7]. What are the coordinates of x relative to the basis C={c1,c2,c3}, where c1=−7b3, c2=2b2 and c3=−b1?

a
[x]C=[−751]
b
[x]C=[15−1]
c
[x]C=[−72−1]
d
[x]C=[110−1]
e
[x]C=[151]
Submit
Incorrect
EXPLANATION

Since [x]B=[110−7], we can write x as follows:

x=b1+10b2−7b3=−7b3+10b2+b1=−7b3+5(2b2)−(−b1)=c1+5c2−c3

Therefore, [x]C=[15−1].

?

Let B={b1,b2,b3} be a basis of R3 and [x]B=[4−68]. What are the coordinates of x relative to the basis C={c1,c2,c3}, where c1=4b3, c2=2b1 and c3=3b2?

a
[x]C=[12−2]
b
[x]C=[212]
c
[x]C=[122]
d
[x]C=[4−22]
e
[x]C=[22−2]
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

Since [x]B=[4−68], we can write x as follows:

x=4b1−6b2+8b3=8b3+4b1−6b2=2(4b3)+2(2b1)−2(3b2)=2c1+2c2−2c3

Therefore, [x]C=[22−2].

q-113095.name: Question 11
q-113095.problem: Let $B=\{{b}_{1},{b}_{2}\}$ be a basis of ${R}^{2}$ and $[x]_{B}=[\begin{aligned}4 \\ -2\end{aligned}].$ What are the coordinates of $x$ relative to the basis $C=\{{c}_{1},{c}_{2}\},$ where ${c}_{1}=2{b}_{1}-{b}_{2}$ and ${c}_{2}={b}_{2}-{b}_{1}?$
q-113095.worked_solution:
We are given that

$$
\{\begin{aligned}{c}_{1}=2{b}_{1}-{b}_{2} \\ {c}_{2}=-{b}_{1}+{b}_{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

First, we express the $b$'s in terms of $c$'s. Adding the equations, we get 

$$
{c}_{1}+{c}_{2}={b}_{1}\,⟹\,{b}_{1}={c}_{1}+{c}_{2}.
$$

Substituting this into the first equation, we obtain

$$
{c}_{1}=2({c}_{1}+{c}_{2})-{b}_{2}\,⟹\,{b}_{2}={c}_{1}+2{c}_{2}.
$$

Since $[x]_{B}=[\begin{aligned}4 \\ -2\end{aligned}]$, we can write the vector $x$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}x & =4{b}_{1}-2{b}_{2} \\  & =4({c}_{1}+{c}_{2})-2({c}_{1}+2{c}_{2}) \\  & =4{c}_{1}+4{c}_{2}-2{c}_{1}-4{c}_{2} \\  & =2{c}_{1}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, $[x]_{C}=[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 0\end{aligned}].$

{c1=2b1−b2c2=−b1+b2.

c1+c2=b1⟹b1=c1+c2.

$$

$$

$$

q-80828.problem: Let $B=\{{b}_{1},{b}_{2}\}$ be a basis of ${R}^{2}$ and $[x]_{B}=[\begin{aligned}-5 \\ 2\end{aligned}].$ What are the coordinates of $x$ relative to the basis $C=\{{c}_{1},{c}_{2}\},$ where ${c}_{1}=3{b}_{2}$ and ${c}_{2}={b}_{1}+6{b}_{2}?$
q-80828.worked_solution:
We are given that

$$
\{\begin{aligned}{c}_{1}=3{b}_{2} \\ {c}_{2}={b}_{1}+6{b}_{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

First, we express the $b$'s in terms of $c$'s. From the first equation, we get 

$$
{b}_{2}=\frac{1}{3}{c}_{1}.
$$

Substituting this into the second equation, we obtain

$$
{c}_{2}={b}_{1}+6(\frac{1}{3}{c}_{1})\,⟹\,{b}_{1}={c}_{2}-2{c}_{1}.
$$

Since $[x]_{B}=[\begin{aligned}-5 \\ 2\end{aligned}]$, we can write the vector $x$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}x & =-5{b}_{1}+2{b}_{2} \\  & =-5({c}_{2}-2{c}_{1})+2(\frac{1}{3}{c}_{1}) \\  & =-5{c}_{2}+10{c}_{1}+\frac{2}{3}{c}_{1} \\  & =\frac{32}{3}{c}_{1}-5{c}_{2}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, $[x]_{C}=[\begin{aligned}\frac{32}{3} \\ -5\end{aligned}].$

a

b

EXPLANATION

{c1=3b2c2=b1+6b2.

b2=13c1.

Substituting this into the second equation, we obtain

c2=b1+6(13c1)⟹b1=c2−2c1.

Since [x]B=[−52], we can write the vector x as follows:

x=−5b1+2b2=−5(c2−2c1)+2(13c1)=−5c2+10c1+23c1=323c1−5c2

q-113070.problem: Let $B=\{{b}_{1},{b}_{2}\}$ be a basis of ${R}^{2}$ and $[x]_{B}=[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 3\end{aligned}].$ What are the coordinates of $x$ relative to the basis $C=\{{c}_{1},{c}_{2}\},$ where ${c}_{1}=2{b}_{1}+{b}_{2}$ and ${c}_{2}=-{b}_{1}?$
q-113070.worked_solution:
We are given that

$$
\{\begin{aligned}{c}_{1}=2{b}_{1}+{b}_{2} \\ {c}_{2}=-{b}_{1}.\end{aligned}
$$

First, we express the $b$'s in terms of $c$'s. From the second equation, we get 

$$
{b}_{1}=-{c}_{2}.
$$

Substituting this into the first equation, we obtain

$$
{c}_{1}=2(-{c}_{2})+{b}_{2}\,⟹\,{b}_{2}={c}_{1}+2{c}_{2}.
$$

Since $[x]_{B}=[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 3\end{aligned}]$, we can write the vector $x$ as follows: 

$$
\begin{aligned}x & =-{b}_{1}+3{b}_{2} \\  & =-(-{c}_{2})+3({c}_{1}+2{c}_{2}) \\  & ={c}_{2}+3{c}_{1}+6{c}_{2} \\  & =7{c}_{2}+3{c}_{1}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, $[x]_{C}=[\begin{aligned}3 \\ 7\end{aligned}].$

q-113098.name: Question 15
q-113098.problem: Let $B=\{{b}_{1},{b}_{2}\}$ be a basis of ${R}^{2}$ and $[x]_{B}=[\begin{aligned}-8 \\ 6\end{aligned}].$ What are the coordinates of $x$ relative to the basis $C=\{{c}_{1},{c}_{2}\},$ where ${c}_{1}=-2{b}_{2}$ and ${c}_{2}=-2{b}_{1}+{b}_{2}?$
q-113098.worked_solution:
We are given that

$$
\{\begin{aligned}{c}_{1}=-2{b}_{2} \\ {c}_{2}=-2{b}_{1}+{b}_{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

First, we express the $b$'s in terms of $c$'s. From the first equation, we get 

$$
{b}_{2}=-\frac{1}{2}{c}_{1}.
$$

Substituting this into the second equation, we obtain

$$
{c}_{2}=-2{b}_{1}+(-\frac{1}{2}{c}_{1})\,⟹\,{b}_{1}=-\frac{1}{4}{c}_{1}-\frac{1}{2}{c}_{2}.
$$

Since $[x]_{B}=[\begin{aligned}-8 \\ 6\end{aligned}]$, we can write the vector $x$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}x & =-8{b}_{1}+6{b}_{2} \\  & =-8(-\frac{1}{4}{c}_{1}-\frac{1}{2}{c}_{2})+6(-\frac{1}{2}{c}_{1}) \\  & =2{c}_{1}+4{c}_{2}-3{c}_{1} \\  & =-{c}_{1}+4{c}_{2}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, $[x]_{C}=[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 4\end{aligned}].$
